newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB predicts A$170-180/t pool price for 97/98.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB predicts A$170-180/t pool price for 97/98.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) believed the pool price for Australian Standard White (ASW) for 1997/98 would be in the A$170-A$180 range, AWB chairman Trevor Flugge told the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) outlook conference on Wednesday.
This compares with the current pool price for ASW of A$192 a tonne.
The AWB is scheduled to release its first 1997/98 pool returns estimate on February 17.
Flugge said he believed there was more upside than downside in the wheat price.
The 1997/98 market for wheat would be characterised by volatility, he said.
Stocks-to-use ratios were still tight and major questions still hung over world markets, he said.
These included northern hemisphere crops, European Union behaviour with export subsidies and what would occur with the U.S. export enhancement programme (EEP), he said.
Earlier, Rhonda Treadwell, manager of ABARE's agriculture branch, predicted 1997/98 world wheat prices at US$170 a tonne nominal against US$180 in 1996/97.
